speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent, and I understand you are a neonate presenting with seizures, lethargy, and other neurological signs three days after birth. To begin our assessment, please tell me: is your mother's pregnancy history remarkable, and did she have any infections like Group B Strep or Zika during her pregnancy?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Sepsis (likely Group B Streptococcus or E. coli) secondary to antenatal chorioamnionitis and prematurity.

I have noted the low birth weight, gestational age, chorioamnionitis, and poor Apgar scores. To confirm the diagnosis, I request: REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture, REQUEST TEST: CSF_Analysis_and_CSF_Culture, REQUEST TEST: Serum_Lactate.
